chunks: And from him, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Jamil ibn Salih, from Muhammad ibn Marwan, who said:

I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'Indeed, for Allah are those freed and released from the Fire every night of the month of Ramadan, except for one who breaks his fast on a intoxicant. And when it is the last night of it, He frees in it as many as He freed in all of it.'

key_terms.عُتَقَاءَ: Freed slaves or those released from bondage

ai.seo_question: How many people are freed from Hellfire during Ramadan according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib* underscores the unique divine generosity of Ramadan, where Allah liberates souls from the Fire nightly, with the exception of those who consume intoxicants. The final night’s reward, equating to the cumulative total of the preceding nights, highlights the concept of *I’tiq* (emancipation) as a central spiritual benefit of the month. This emphasis on consistent devotion, punctuated by the specific exclusion of intoxicants, reflects the Shia scholarly focus on both ritual purity and spiritual liberation.
